source.title: Enhancing Jailbreak Attacks with Diversity Guidance
source.authors: Xu Zhang; Ding-Hao Jing; Xiao-Jun Wan

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether optimized adversarial suffixes can elicit harmful responses from safety-oriented models, using jailbreak attack-success measures rather than the original studies’ fine-tuning or token-position measurements.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are suffix-based jailbreak outcomes on harmful-behavior prompts and risk-boundary measurements under DSTS. The paper also reports harmful-string generation, but that is not the harmful-request compliance behavior named by the versions. The authors state substring matching overestimates harmful-behavior attack success; the GPT-3.5-turbo evaluation is the more direct measure. No results test fine-tuning, token-position KL, compliant prefilling, or safety localization in weights.
record.test_reason: The paper measures how often optimized adversarial suffixes get safety-trained chat models to give harmful responses on AdvBench, judged by GPT-3.5-turbo. That bears on V4's claim that suffixes defeat refusal. It does not test prefilling, decoding changes, fine-tuning, KL concentration or localization. It also cites Qi et al. only as the source of HEx-PHI.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say DSTS improves optimized jailbreaks through diversity guidance and that risk boundaries vary by model and domain. They also stress that substring matching overestimates success.
record.recipe_differences: The study optimizes adversarial suffix triggers with gradient-based search and DPP selection; it does not use fine-tuning or test response-token KL concentration or compliant-opening prefills.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies with model, attack algorithm, evaluation judge, target model for transferred triggers, and HEx-PHI domain. The paper specifically notes that substring matching overestimates harmful-behavior success compared with GPT-3.5-turbo evaluation.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The authors note limited model size and experimental settings. Substring matching is acknowledged to overestimate harmful-behavior success; the more direct GPT-3.5-turbo evaluation yields substantially lower rates. Risk boundaries use DSTS as an approximation to an optimal attack, not exhaustive adversarial-prompt enumeration.
record.rows_left_out: Table 6 reports 99 HEx-PHI model-by-domain risk-boundary values; 12 selected high- and low-value conditions are included and the other 87 are omitted due to the 60-row limit. Table 1 substring-matching rows are retained but not used as decisive verdict evidence because the authors say that metric overestimates success. The Table 3 transfer-rate values are omitted because they are transfer proportions rather than direct harmful-response rates.

untested.parts: Compliant-start prefilling and decoding changes were not tested.

missing.what: Table 6 risk-boundary values for LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, LLaMA-2-13B and others, to compare models. Only 12 of 99 cells are recorded.
Harmful-string results (CivilComments Tox-1 to Tox-3), a related but different measure.

record.verdict_notes: The T1 LLaMA LLM-judged rows appear shifted by one column against Table 1 (the extracted values sit under the wrong methods), so the row values need re-extraction. In Table 1, the 'LLM' column for LLaMA reads 0.00, 10.79, 30.96, 31.54, 34.23, 37.50, 42.31 and the 'Matching' column reads 0.00, 58.46, 45.00, 93.65, 56.15, 96.92, 100. The extracted pairs shift one slot. The V4 'challenges' label from the reader is not supported. High risk-boundary cells reflect a single attack at a fixed budget, not a failure of V4, and they are sub-cells picked from Table 6. The paper reports no uncertainty or seeds for the single-run results. All tested models are about 7B-70B, none was fine-tuned, and the study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Tests optimized adversarial suffixes, not compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether the data or objective used in safety training produces shallowness.
Training to deepen safety and whether the effect persists.

relationships.condition: Optimized suffix attacks (DSTS, GCG, AutoPrompt) on LLaMA-2-7B-Chat and Vicuna-7B, judged by GPT-3.5-turbo
relationships.reason: Strong attacks yield harmful outputs on about 31-45% of AdvBench prompts (T1-L-DSTS-J, T1-V-DSTS-J, T2-L-FULL-J, T2-V-FULL-J), and the DSTS ablations rise with each component (Table 2). The authors treat the LLM-judged figures as the valid measure.
relationships.display_finding: The strongest attacks produced harmful outputs on about 31–45% of AdvBench prompts, and the DSTS ablations improved with each added component; the authors treat the LLM-judged figures as the valid measure.

relationships.condition: LLM-judged success is well under the substring-match figures; transfer to larger models and several HEx-PHI domains is limited
relationships.reason: LLM-judged ASR tops out near 45% versus 100% by substring match. Transfer to 70B drops to 20.58% (T3-L70-ASR) and 33.85% on Vicuna-33B (T3-V33-ASR). Weak attacks (GBDA, PGDC) score near zero on Vicuna.
relationships.display_finding: LLM-judged attack success topped out near 45%, against 100% by substring match. Transfer fell to 20.58% on a 70B model and 33.85% on Vicuna-33B, and the weaker GBDA and PGDC attacks scored near zero on Vicuna.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-3.5-turbo evaluations of optimized suffix attacks on AdvBench harmful instructions
reader_labels.reason: The suffix attacks produce outputs judged harmful, with reported success rates from 10.79% to 44.81%, across models and attack methods (T1-L-GBDA-J through T1-V-DSTS-J).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT-3.5-turbo evaluations on AdvBench and transfer targets
reader_labels.reason: Harmful completion rates are partial rather than near-total, and transfer success varies by target; substring matching gives much higher values but the authors warn that it overestimates success (Table 1 and Table 3 rows).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Selected HEx-PHI domains and models with high risk-boundary values under DSTS
reader_labels.reason: Risk-boundary values of 0.90 or higher indicate that most queries remained safe under the study’s definition, in these tested conditions (H-L3-ILL, H-GEM-CHILD, H-GEM-FIN, H-L3-CHILD).
